articles.title: Eight Choices. One Team. One Long Night. Our first hackathon: learning, problem-solving, and building together
articles.excerpt: At 4 p.m., we set off for the auditorium full of excitement—and already hungry and impatient to begin. This was our first hackathon, and all three of us were eager to get started. But before the build…
articles.body: At 4 p.m., we set off for the auditorium full of excitement—and already hungry and impatient to begin. This was our first hackathon, and all three of us were eager to get started. But before the building could begin, there was a lot to take in. We spent two hours listening to the panellists, and came away with more ideas and learning than we had expected. One piece of advice stayed with me: ask AI “why.” Asking why can help you understand the reasoning behind an answer. Jump straight to “how” before you understand the problem, and you may find yourself going around in circles. That idea would soon feel relevant as our team faced its first big question: which problem should we solve?
articles.author: yuvraj

articles.title: WARN Act and Non-Compete Agreements: What a Layoff Does (and Doesn't Do) to Your Non-Compete
articles.excerpt: When a WARN notice lands, most workers focus on the urgent questions: when does the job end, when does the last paycheck arrive, and what happens to health coverage. A quieter question often surfaces…
articles.body: When a WARN notice lands, most workers focus on the urgent questions: when does the job end, when does the last paycheck arrive, and what happens to health coverage. A quieter question often surfaces days later: does the layoff cancel the non-compete you signed when hired? The short answer is no, not automatically. A WARN notice announces a planned layoff; it is not a release from other contracts. Whether your non-compete still binds you depends on the wording of your own agreement, the law of the state that governs it, and sometimes how you lost your job. These are reported plans, not confirmed job losses, and the same caution applies to every filing discussed here: WARN figures describe what employers have reported, and plans can change.

articles.title: Twelve Hours, Four Friends, and a Whole Lot of Coffee: Our Hack Day Journey
articles.excerpt: There’s a unique kind of chaos that only hits you at 3:00 AM in a room full of glowing screens and buzzing energy. That was us—Team CodeSins—deep into Hack Day Sonipat, wondering why on earth we thoug…
articles.body: There’s a unique kind of chaos that only hits you at 3:00 AM in a room full of glowing screens and buzzing energy. That was us—Team CodeSins—deep into Hack Day Sonipat, wondering why on earth we thought building a massive puzzle in just twelve hours was a good idea. Led by Pulkit Goel, alongside Vibhav Maurya, Uday Saha, and Nischay Jain, our little crew started the night with big dreams, plenty of snacks, and a ticking clock that felt way too loud. The hurdles started hitting us almost immediately. Building something from absolute scratch means dealing with a mountain of moving parts, and let me tell you, things will break. At one point, half our puzzle pieces wouldn't talk to the other half, and every time someone tried to fix a section, another corner seemed to fall apart.

articles.body: Stop building simple RAG bots that just summarize PDFs. The future of AI is Agentic workflows that can reason, loop, and take action based on real-time physiological data. If you’ve been looking to dive into LangGraph , AI Agents , and HealthKit integration , you’re in the right place. In this tutorial, we are building a "Smart Recovery Agent." Instead of just telling you to "work out harder," this agent analyzes your Heart Rate Variability (HRV) —the gold standard for recovery—and uses a state machine to dynamically adjust your training volume and fetch personalized nutrition plans via Tavily Search . This is a leap forward in Fitness AI and LLM state management . Why LangGraph? 🧠 Traditional chains are linear. But health is cyclical and conditional.

articles.title: AI Made Building Easier. Getting Your First 10 Users Is Still Hard.
articles.excerpt: A few months ago, I started building a project called Critique. The idea was simple: give developers and indie makers a place to share what they're building, ask one focused question, and get honest f…
articles.body: A few months ago, I started building a project called Critique. The idea was simple: give developers and indie makers a place to share what they're building, ask one focused question, and get honest feedback from real people. I thought building the product would be the biggest challenge. I was wrong. Building software is getting easier AI tools have changed how developers work. Today, you can: Generate a frontend in minutes. Build APIs with AI assistance. Debug code faster. Create prototypes without a large team. As a solo developer, I use these tools to move faster. But there's a problem. Building something doesn't mean people will use it. You can have a working application, a clean interface, and a long list of features, but still struggle to find your first users.

Digital Foundry’s analysis of the performance of the Switch 2 version of Modern Warfare 4 — the first Call of Duty released on a Nintendo console since 2013’s Ghosts — found that the input lag on Switch 2 can be two times longer than on PS5 at 60fps. articles.excerpt: Anakin Skywalker actor Hayden Christensen has revealed the strangest fan encounter he’s ever had.
articles.body: Anakin Skywalker actor Hayden Christensen has revealed the strangest fan encounter he’s ever had. Speaking on stage at L.A. Comic Con, as reported by The Nerd Wire , the Star Wars veteran said that years ago, a burglar recognized him during a robbery at his home, apologized, then gave his stuff back. Christensen was upstairs when he heard the door open, and when he found the burglar, he was holding his belongings. “I’m like, is this a delivery guy?” Christensen was quoted as saying. “And I look and I’m like, this is all my stuff.” Remarkably, Christensen then offered to buy the man who broke into his house a train ticket home. No, a Jedi mind trick hadn’t caused the burglar to have a surprise change of heart. He just happened to be a fan who decided on a quick U-turn.

articles.excerpt: On October 31, 2015, an asteroid shaped like a human skull flew by Earth. Here's why it was so creepy.
articles.body: On October 31, 2015, an asteroid shaped like a human skull flew by Earth. It arrived with excellent timing on Halloween, which made the already-creepy asteroid even creepier. During its closest approach, the creepy asteroid was about 300,000 miles from Earth, or 1.3 times the average distance between Earth and the moon . So, it didn't pose a threat to our planet. It was discovered by astronomers at Hawaii's Pan-STARRS observatory only three weeks before the flyby, and it was given the official designation "2015 TB145." But no one knew what it looked like until the day before Halloween, when the Arecibo Observatory in Puerto Rico captured the first radar images.

articles.title: The moon, Mars, and Jupiter shine in the heart of the Lion overnight on Nov. 1-2
articles.excerpt: The waning moon shines with Jupiter, Mars and the brilliant star Regulus in the eastern sky overnight Nov. 1-2.
articles.body: The moon dives towards the glowing heart of the constellation Leo for a spectacular rendezvous with Mars and Jupiter overnight on Nov. 1-2, as the glittering stars of the Beehive Cluster shine nearby. Here's what you need to know. Look to the eastern horizon an hour after midnight to see the 45%-lit waning moon shining less than 5 degrees from the red light of Mars — roughly the width of your three middle fingers held at arm's length to the night sky. Jupiter's bright light will gleam just below the red planet, with the bright star Regulus lining up beyond to form a dazzling procession leading back to the horizon. The stars of the Beehive Cluster (M44) can be found twinkling 10 degrees from the unlit side of the lunar disk around this time, in the middle of the constellation Cancer .

articles.title: Betelgeuse is haunted by a cosmic poltergeist tormenting the doomed star's atmosphere
articles.excerpt: Radio images show the supergiant's atmosphere recovering from its dramatic dimming, while a companion plows through its outer layers.
articles.body: Something spooky is stirring in the shadows of the infamous star Betelgeuse, a cosmic poltergeist that is disrupting the atmosphere of the red supergiant. New radio observations have shown Betelgeuse's smaller stellar companion, Siwarha (not Betelguese Betelguese, unfortunately), cutting through the supergiant's extended atmosphere and leaving a wake in its path, like a jet boat slicing through a lake.

articles.title: Anthropic VS code extension on Cursor backdoored for nearly 12 hours
articles.excerpt: It's still unknown how attackers got access to Anthropic's verified Cursor account.
articles.body: An official extension for Anthropic’s Claude model was backdoored and threatened as many as 5,000 developers' machines, multiple sources reported Friday. Anthropic so far has yet to warn customers of the incident. The compromised package was a VS Code extension available in the marketplace of Cursor, a maker of AI-assisted developer tools, the company said Friday. The malicious version, 2.1.313, subsequently affected “at most 5,000 users,” presumably when they either downloaded it or their systems automatically fetched and installed it. Anthropic pushed version 2.1.314 several hours after the previous version became available on Cursor, according to independent researcher Kevin Beaumont.
